predecessors.name: Lê dynasty
predecessors.text: Đàng Ngoài, the Lê court's north (Thanh Hóa, Nghệ An and Hà Tĩnh) under the Trịnh lords

successors.name: Tây Sơn dynasty
successors.text: the north (Tonkin), taken by the Tây Sơn after the Trịnh fell

ledger.x: 1572: the Trịnh lords stand at the head of the Lê court's north.
1573: the Mạc retake the capital 'a year later'; the page has no month.
1592: the Lê-Trịnh army marches on Đông Kinh.
1592: Đông Kinh and the northern provinces pass from the Mạc to the Trịnh-led Lê court.
1592: the capital returns to Đông Kinh (Hanoi).
April 1593: the Lê emperor returns to Đông Kinh.
1656: the Nguyễn are 'pushed back to their original walls' and Hà Tĩnh returns to the Trịnh.
1677: the Trịnh destroy the Mạc rump in Cao Bằng.
15 November 1774: Trịnh Sâm attacks the Nguyễn and, 'for the first time', the Nguyễn walls are broken, ending a truce of about a hundred years.
1775: Nguyễn Nhạc becomes a Trịnh official.
1775: Thuận Hóa passes to a Trịnh viceroy.
1778: Nguyễn Nhạc proclaims himself emperor ('Nguyễn Nhạc, proclaimed himself Emperor in 1778'), ending his place as a Trịnh official.
1786: the Tây Sơn take Phú Xuân.

wars.name: Lê–Mạc War
wars.outcome: Revival Lê and Trịnh victory: Đông Kinh reconquered in 1592, the Mạc rump in Cao Bằng 'completely defeated by the Trịnh clan in 1677'.

wars.name: Trịnh–Nguyễn War (first phase)
wars.outcome: Indecisive: open warfare from 1627, offensives in 1633, 1642-43, 1648, 1661 and 1671 failed against the walls; the Nguyễn invaded in 1653 and were pushed back by 1656; peace in 1673 'mediated by the Kangxi Emperor's government' with the Linh River as the…

wars.name: Trịnh–Nguyễn War (second phase)
wars.outcome: Trịnh and Tây Sơn victory: the Trịnh captured Phú Xuân in February 1775 and the Nguyễn retreated to Quảng Nam and later to Gia Định; the Trịnh left the destruction of the Nguyễn to the southern rebels.

wars.name: Tây Sơn campaign against the Trịnh
wars.outcome: Tây Sơn victory: Phú Xuân and Thăng Long fell in 1786, Trịnh Tông died and the lords were restored only briefly under Trịnh Bồng, who fell to Nguyễn Hữu Chỉnh in fall 1787.

certainty.note: The Mạc front, the Cham-Nguyễn walls and the Lao and Chinese uplands are approximate.

The southern frontier with the Nguyễn is the line of the 1673 peace ('strongly guarded but peaceful'; the Gianh or Linh River) and is the one sharp border, but the Cao Bằng, Lao and Qing frontiers stay soft, so the era is soft.
The Thuận Hóa viceroyalty and Nhạc's client land have no stated lines.
